review_comments.body: resolveGroup returns group.getId() which is the same as the input id and is used as the resource name. The rest of the code expects a human readable name / the resource name built from the group id, so getOrCreateResource will create resources with an id as name and later lookups will be inconsistent. The method should return a stable name, e.g. the group name or the prefixed resource name used elsewhere.

hasPermission looks up a group resource with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Group resources are stored with name RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX + groupId, so findByName with the raw groupId will never find the resource. This makes all per-group permission checks in V2 silently fail and falls back to the all-groups resource. Use the prefixed name or findById.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission now returns an empty set only when root.users().canView() is true. The previous implementation also short-circuited on root.users().canManage(). Removing the canManage check changes the semantics: a user with MANAGE_USERS but without VIEW_USERS will now be treated as restricted and will receive a group filter, which can incorrectly hide users.

review_comments.body: enable_advanced checks organization_context.member.has_global_access without guarding for member being None, which can raise AttributeError for non-members. Also exposing an experimental paginator via request.GET['optimized_pagination'] increases attack surface for privileged users.

self.paginate is called with enable_advanced_features=True. The paginate helper does not forward arbitrary kwargs to the paginator constructor, so the flag is ignored or raises TypeError, making the optimized path ineffective/unsafe.

DateTimePaginator.get_result now allows negative start_offset for prev cursors: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. Negative slicing on a Django QuerySet is not safe and can cause incorrect results, full scans, or errors; the comment claiming ORM handles it is incorrect.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/ceil to getattr(item, self.key). For DateTimePaginator the key is a datetime, so math.floor/ceil will raise TypeError. The method is incompatible with non-numeric cursor keys.

When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0 the paginator slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset. This bypasses the cursor-based filtering built by build_queryset, can return out-of-bounds rows, and enables DoS via large/negative slices. Negative offsets are not a safe performance optimization.

Cursor.__init__ now documents allowing negative offsets but does not validate them. Unrestricted negative offsets propagate to paginators and can be used to construct malformed cursors that break pagination invariants and leak data.

This adds attack surface and couples audit log endpoint to experimental paginator changes.

DateTimePaginator.get_result now allows negative start_offset for prev cursors: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. Negative queryset slicing is unsafe in Django and can lead to incorrect results, data leakage or DoS via large scans.

OptimizedCursorPaginator enables negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features` is true and uses `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django ORM does not safely support negative slicing and this bypasses pagination limits, risking unbounded queries.
Redirect loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000. The comment notes depth 10k may be needed for segment tree joins; lowering to 1000 can cause incorrect parent resolution for deep traces.

Switch from `sunionstore` to `zunionstore` with default AGGREGATE SUM. If the same payload member exists in both sets, scores are summed instead of preserved/deduped, corrupting the timestamp ordering used for eviction.

`span_count` is overwritten by the second `zunionstore` for parent_key, so eviction `zpopmin` is based only on the parent union result, not total set size. This can leave the set over the 1000-item limit.
`_load_segment_data` now uses `zscan` but removed the `max_segment_spans` enforcement block. Without the span count cap, a segment can grow unbounded in memory during flush, risking OOM.

review_comments.body: Calling I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in set_locale runs on every request. ensure_loaded! loads the current locale and all fallbacks each time, which adds I/O and CPU overhead even when locales are already loaded. Consider loading once at boot or guarding with a loaded check.

FallbackLocaleList#[] accesses SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym on every fallback lookup. SiteSetting hits the DB and this method is invoked for each translation, causing repeated DB reads and breaking the expectation that fallbacks is a static mapping. Memoize the default locale or read it once at runtime.

I18n.ensure_loaded! is not part of the public I18n API. The custom ensure_loaded! is defined on the TranslateAccelerator backend instance, so I18n.ensure_loaded! may not delegate correctly and can raise NoMethodError. Use I18n.backend.ensure_loaded! or expose the method on I18n explicitly.

ensure_loaded! mutates @loaded_locales without synchronization. Under concurrent requests the check `unless @loaded_locales.include?(locale)` can race, leading to duplicate loads or missed loads. Consider thread-safe guarding or using I18n's built-in loading semantics.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/7.pr_title: Comprehensive workflow reminder management for booking lifecycle events

review_comments.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are invoked inside forEach without await, resulting in fire-and-forget promises and unhandled rejections. The previous scheduled && referenceId guard was removed, so unscheduled reminders are also processed.

When immediateDelete is false the function only updates workflowReminder.cancelled=true and does not cancel the scheduled send with the provider. The email can still be delivered until the hourly cleanup job runs, changing the previous immediate cancel behavior.

remindersToCancel fetches WorkflowReminder with cancelled=true without filtering by method. The subsequent POST to /v3/user/scheduled_sends and delete is email-specific, so SMS reminders will be incorrectly processed and deleted.
The wrapper condition was changed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only, removing the sender ID UI block. SMS sender ID configuration is now unreachable.

Cancellation of workflow reminders for a rescheduled booking uses forEach with async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls that are not awaited. ImmediateDelete is passed for email but not for SMS, leading to inconsistent cleanup and potential orphaned reminders.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/8.pr_title: Async import of the appStore packages

review_comments.body: Array.forEach with an async callback is not awaited. The await getCalendar and calendar?.deleteEvent calls run fire-and-forget, so errors are unhandled and deletions may not complete before the function returns. Use for...of with await or Promise.all.
Array.forEach with an async callback is not awaited. getCalendar and deleteEvent promises are not awaited, leading to race conditions and unhandled rejections. Replace with for...of or Promise.all.

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) does not await the async work. The await getCalendar and calendar?.deleteEvent calls are fire-and-forget. This can cause missed deletions and swallowed errors. Use for...of with await or Promise.all.

getCalendar is now async but is called without await here. calendar becomes a Promise, which is later awaited as item.calendar. Await getCalendar at the source to avoid double-await and confusing types.

forEach(async (credential) => { ... await getCalendar ... }) is not awaited. The async iteration is fire-and-forget, so calendar updates/deletes may not finish before the handler completes. Use for...of with await or collect promises with Promise.all.
